title: Primitive recursion: functions built by finite iteration

based_on.title: An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems
based_on.pages: 96–104, 106–112 (§§14.1–14.4 and 14.6–14.7; second edition, corrected reprint August 2020)

summary: Build numerical functions from composition and finite iteration, then prove that bounded tests and bounded searches stay within the same class.
abstract: To multiply two natural numbers, we can repeatedly add; to raise a number to a power, we can repeatedly multiply. Primitive recursion turns this familiar pattern into a precise way of building functions, starting with zero, successor and the selection of an input. Every function obtained this way has a value at every input. The same construction also handles finite sums, tests for equality and order, and searches whose range is specified in advance. We prove these closure properties by giving the recursions explicitly, including what happens when a search finds nothing. As an application, division with remainder can be performed by a bounded search. The point is to distinguish a function's mathematical description from the finite recipe that establishes how it can be calculated.
